newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sega says sees domestic game sales rising 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sega says sees domestic game sales rising 30 pct.

text.p: Sega Enterprises Ltd said on Thursday it expects domestic game software sales to grow by at least one-third this year.
"We expect at least 30 percent growth in software sales in Japan," Sega executive vice-president Shoichiro Irimajiri told Reuters.
A Sega spokesman said Irimajiri's estimate referred to a year-on-year increase for the year to March 31, 1998.
Sega on Thursday unveiled its "Sakura Wars 2", a new software title for its 32-bit Sega Saturn game machine. Sega plans to be release the game title around March 1998 in Japan.
"I believe this software has the possibility of selling a million copies," Irimajiri told a news conference.
Irimajiri said his estimate of software sales growth included sales of the new software.
Irimajiri said the company was studying the possibility of selling the game overseas. "The Sakura Wars series would attract consumers in the United States," he said.
Sales of Sega's software titles for Saturn machines totalled 25 million units in Japan in 1996/97, the Sega spokesman said.
In May, Sega said it would shift its focus to the profitable software sector from the loss-making hardware sector in 1997/98.
